description: When Dean has all required info, [READY] response must not also ask an open question

conversation_history.content: Hey! I'm Coach Dean — AI running coach, personalized plans, Strava sync, SMS check-ins. What's your name?
Jake. Training for Cirque Series Snowbird in July — mountain trail race, 8.9 miles.
Snowbird is a serious mountain race — love it. Which days work best for training?
Tuesday through Thursday, Saturday and Sunday.

Five days — solid base to work with. I can see your training history if you connect Strava, or just tell me a recent race time or easy run pace.

https://coachdean.ai/api/auth/strava?userId=abc123

No Strava? Just reply "skip".
No worries. What's your current easy run pace, or a recent race time I can use to set your training zones?
My easy pace is around 9:30 per mile. I'm in Provo, Utah.

strava_context: STRAVA: User skipped Strava. Collect mileage + pace data manually.
inbound_message: My easy pace is around 9:30 per mile. I'm in Provo, Utah.

ground_truth.notes: Dean now has everything required: name, goal (trail_race / Cirque Series Snowbird), race date, training days, easy pace, and location/timezone. He should signal [READY] at the end of his response. Crucially, if he signals [READY], he must NOT also ask a question in the same message. The correct behavior is a warm wrap-up like 'Perfect — I have everything I need, I'll put your plan together now. [READY]'. The known failure mode: Dean asks 'Do you have a goal finish time?' AND signals [READY] in the same message — this causes the plan to fire while the question is left unanswered.
